source.title: Disorders of compulsivity: Deficits in arbitrating learning strategies.

confidence_rationale: Empirically dissociates the locus of the compulsivity deficit: across OCD, alcohol-use-disorder and depression patients fitted with model-based/model-free RL, OCD patients specifically showed excess system-SWITCHING (an arbitration/control-mechanism failure) rather than only reduced model-based use. This directly supports Q-063's core conjecture that compulsive stickiness can arise from a biased control/arbitration landscape rather than from genuine value -- the field-state-driven-stickiness limb of the question. Strong because it isolates arbitration as a separable locus; held below 0.8 because 'arbitration switching' is REE's MECH-369 decommit-friction analogue only by mapping, and the offline-integration leg is untouched.
failure_signatures: OCD patients showed HIGHER behavioural-control system switching where consistent model-free use was optimal -- a control-layer abnormality decoupled from value; a REE diagnostic that reads only z_goal/value would misclassify such a loop as low-value rather than seeing the arbitration/decommit-friction bias.

Major depressive disorder patients did NOT show the arbitration deficit -- so the signature is specific to compulsivity disorders, warning that not every persistent loop is modulator-trapped; the diagnostic must discriminate compulsive stickiness from other persistence causes.

mapping.source_claim_statement: OCD and alcohol-use-disorder patients showed less model-based strategy choice where it was optimal, but ONLY OCD patients showed higher behavioural-control system switching where model-free use was optimal; major depression patients differed on neither -- implicating dysfunction of the ARBITRATION mechanism (which system controls behaviour at each moment), not just a single-system deficit, as the basis of compulsivity.
mapping.ree_translation: Direct support for the field-state-driven-stickiness limb of Q-063: compulsive persistence can be driven by a biased arbitration/control mechanism (the analogue of REE's decommit-friction / threshold landscape, MECH-369) rather than by the value of the goal. The 'system switching' abnormality is a behavioural fingerprint of control-landscape bias decoupled from value.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's 'arbitration mechanism' is a model-based/model-free meta-controller, not REE's slow-modulator field biasing decommit-friction; the mapping is functional (control-layer bias independent of value) not mechanistic. The study is correlational across patient groups, not a causal manipulation of the arbitration bias.
mapping.source_context: Human patients: 19 alcohol-use-disorder, 30 OCD, 20 major depression + matched controls, performing a 2-choice 3-stage Markov decision task fitted with model-based/model-free RL.

confidence_components.notes: Clean clinical dissociation with a discriminant control group (depression null); mapping_fidelity moderate because 'arbitration switching' maps to MECH-369 functionally, not mechanistically.
